title: Unmeasured Thread Spinning on I/O Operations
pattern: Implementing an active spin loop to await network socket data, disk I/O, or OS-level file operations.
why_bad: While spinning avoids thread scheduling latency, I/O operations are fundamentally slow (milliseconds). Spinning for milliseconds burns millions of CPU cycles, wastes energy, and starves other active threads [111, 410].
detection: A tight `while` polling loop awaiting a response from an external network stream, socket, or file descriptor.
counterexample: Graphics processing or extremely high-speed memory bus monitoring where wait times are mathematically guaranteed to be < 100 ns. `Contextual`.
fix: Use standard asynchronous event loops (`tokio` in Rust) or standard blocking read calls with OS-backed thread parking.
